title: Compatibility cohort maintenance for tokenizer, context window, and toolchain parity
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: As smart routing chooses fallback model variants across regions and tiers, several customer incidents and internal integration tests show subtle incompatibilities between variants: tokenizer tokenization differences, mismatched maximum context handling (KV cache limits / context truncation), and tool-calling / function signature mismatches. These differences cause incorrect reroutes, cache misses, garbled structured outputs, and occasional runtime errors in multi-variant fallback chains.

Goal: Maintain a compact, machine-readable compatibility cohort (matrix) that captures tokenizer parity, context-window equivalence, and tooling (function-calling/structured-output) compatibility for all active model variants. Provide a repeatable maintenance workflow: automated checks, triage steps, remediation templates, and release gating so smart-routing fallbacks are only allowed between compatible cohorts.

Scope: Inventory and ongoing maintenance for hosted+dedicated variants in production and canary pools across all regions. Not included: offline research-only model forks or unreleased experimental quantizations.

Success metrics: reduction in fallback-induced errors (target: -75% within one release), zero regressions in end-to-end tool-call tests for routed fallbacks, automated cohort checks run in CI for all deploys to runtime-1.19.
acceptance_criteria: A compact compatibility cohort file (CSV+JSON manifest) stored in /infra/model-compat/compat-cohorts/runtime-1.19 is generated and reviewed
Automated tokenizer parity checks added to variant CI that run on PRs that touch model onboarding or tokenizer configs
Context-window/kv-cache compatibility test added to the routing integration suite with pass/fail thresholds
Tooling/function-call parity smoke tests (3 canonical prompts) included in the canary pipeline; failures block canary promotion
Runbook and remediation checklist committed to Confluence and referenced from the cohort manifest
Routing control plane reads the cohort manifest and refuses to configure fallbacks across incompatible cohorts by default
changes: Create cohort manifest schema (fields: model_variant, tokenizer_hash, max_context, kv_behaviour, tool_call_contracts, last_tested)
Implement tokenizer parity script (tokenize-diff) that compares tokenization outputs for canonical prompts
Extend integration tests to include cross-variant prefix-resumption and kv-cache reuse scenarios
Add gating logic to routing service to check cohort manifest during route update/rollout
Author remediation templates: re-quantize candidate, vendor tokenizer patch, or disable fallback path
Schedule weekly triage rotation for the next 3 sprints to review cohort drift and PRs
rollout_plan: Week 0 (this ticket): finalize manifest schema and add initial cohort for runtime-1.19 with top 12 production variants
Week 1: land tokenizer parity CI job and run against existing variants; triage failures
Week 2: land routing gate that consults the manifest in staging clusters and run end-to-end canary
Week 3: once staging is stable for 48h, flip the gate for a small subset of routing updates in prod (5% traffic)
Week 4: expand to full rollout if no regressions; deprecate any variant that cannot be made compatible within plan
test_plan: Tokenizer parity: 200 canonical prompts across markup/emoji/code paths; diff thresholds and token alignment checks
Context window: sequential request test that validates KV reuse against a golden run within +/-1 token at truncation boundaries
Tooling parity: 3 function-calling scenarios (sync, streaming partial results, complex nested structures) validated end-to-end
Chaos test: simulate region routing fallback and validate end-to-end session consistency (no JSON schema breakage)
Performance: ensure cohort checks add <5ms median to route evaluation path; if >20ms, move to async enforcement
notes: This ticket intentionally scopes to maintenance and automation; larger remediation work (retraining/re-tokenizing models) will spawn follow-ups
Keep cohort manifest small and machine-queriable; avoid human-only spreadsheets
If a variant is temporarily incompatible, routing should prefer region/tier-compatible alternatives rather than forced cross-cohort fallbacks
Align with release-ops before changing routing gate behavior during high-traffic events
